topics.title: Neural Networks from Scratch
topics.description: Build, train, and understand a multi-layer neural network using only the linear algebra, calculus, and statistics you have mastered.
objectives: Represent a neural network as a composition of affine transformations and activations
Derive the backpropagation algorithm using the chain rule
Implement gradient descent and mini-batch SGD
Explain the role of eigenvalues in understanding loss landscapes and weight initialisation
Apply the central limit theorem to justify batch normalisation

problem_templates.prompt_template: A single-layer network maps ℝ³ → ℝ² via z = Wx + b, then applies σ(z) element-wise. Given W = [[1,0,−1],[0,2,1]] and b = [1,−1], compute the output for x = [2,1,3] and the Jacobian ∂z/∂x.
Derive the gradient ∂L/∂W for a two-layer network with MSE loss L = ½||y − ŷ||². Use the chain rule step-by-step, identifying the roles of the activation's derivative and the upstream gradient.

Explain why the Hessian's eigenvalues determine the curvature of the loss landscape and how this motivates adaptive learning rates (Adam). Sketch the relationship between a large condition number and slow gradient descent convergence.
